root_cause.text: The TI k3-socinfo driver’s probe path created an mmio `regmap` with `regmap_init_mmio()` in `k3_chipinfo_probe()` but did not tie it to device-managed cleanup, so any probe failure or driver unbind leaked the allocated regmap object.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `regmap = regmap_init_mmio(dev, base, &k3_chipinfo_regmap_cfg);` to `devm_regmap_init_mmio(dev, base, &k3_chipinfo_regmap_cfg);`, and the commit message explicitly says “The mmio regmap allocated during probe is never freed” and that the devm allocator is needed so it is released on “probe failures (e.g. probe deferral) and on driver unbind.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Convert regmap allocation to device-managed lifetime management to ensure automatic cleanup on device removal.
intent_record.what: In k3_chipinfo_probe(), the regmap initialization call was changed from regmap_init_mmio(dev, base, &k3_chipinfo_regmap_cfg) to devm_regmap_init_mmio(dev, base, &k3_chipinfo_regmap_cfg).
intent_record.how: The regmap is now managed by the device-managed resource framework, so it will be automatically released when the device is detached, instead of requiring explicit cleanup. This reduces the risk of resource leaks and simplifies teardown.

grouping_result.intent: Convert regmap allocation to device-managed lifetime management to ensure automatic cleanup on device removal.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the reported leak by changing the regmap allocation to device-managed lifetime management, which ensures cleanup on probe failure or driver removal.

candidates.rationale: This allocates the MMIO regmap with plain regmap_init_mmio(), but the result is not device-managed, so the regmap can leak on probe failure or driver removal.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement allocates the MMIO regmap using plain regmap_init_mmio() during probe, but it is not tied to device-managed cleanup. As a result, probe failure or driver unbind could leak the regmap object, matching the root cause.
